claims.statement: The guide applies to FPT, GHES and GHEC. Its generic email-already-in-use section says the address is linked to another account and asserts one-account association; this must not erase its later managed-user exception.

Generic recovery instructs signing into the linked account and removing the address, or requesting password reset if access is missing. A reset request is not proof of recovered access or permission to alter someone else's account.

An employer-provided address may already belong to an enterprise managed user; the guide directs the user to internal administrators or helpdesk and suggests IdP application access. Product metadata does not guarantee such an identity deployment exists.

For personal-account reuse, the guide says to sign into the managed user and unverify the address while retaining linkage and IdP access. This reinforces DOCS-EMAILIDENTITY-6 but conflicts with the guide's generic one-account wording; exact scope still requires reconciliation.

Unverified managed email may impair third-party services; continued IdP access is not universal third-party identity verification. No address removal, unverification, password reset or administrator contact is performed.
